simple: a wavefront of 64 lanes or of 32 lanes, fixed when the kernel is compiled.
analogy: a long row or a short row of the same helpers.
precise: the wavefront size a kernel is compiled for, recorded as .wavefront_size in the kernel metadata; in this build gfx90a compiles to 64, gfx1030 and gfx1100 default to 32, and -mwavefrontsize64 selects 64 on RDNA targets (compiler output, F7-08 R2, F7-09 R2). HIP 5.7's header rejects wave64 device compilation for targets other than gfx8/gfx9.
source: D4 of F7-09 (AMD RDNA ISA reference guides) and LLVM AMDGPU user guide — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); compiler output of this build

simple: the number of lanes in a wave, as a name your code can use.
analogy: the number painted at the start of every row.
precise: in HIP 5.7 device code, static constexpr int warpSize = __AMDGCN_WAVEFRONT_SIZE, fixed per compiled target; on the host, hipDeviceProp_t::warpSize.
source: HIP 5.7 header amd_detail/amd_warp_functions.h (read in this build)

simple: the part of a CU that performs the vector instructions of the waves assigned to it.
analogy: one supervisor's counter inside a section: the rows assigned to it take turns there.
precise: a vector execution unit with its own wave slots and its own share of the vector register file; a CU contains several, and AMD occupancy is counted in waves per SIMD. The count per CU is a product fact to take from the architecture documents.
source: D2 of F7-08 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the low 32-bit halves of the vector-condition and execution mask registers, used by wave32 code.
analogy: the left half of a row's attendance sheet, all that a short row needs.
precise: VCC and EXEC are 64-bit registers made of two 32-bit halves; wave32 code uses vcc_lo and exec_lo, wave64 code the full pair (assembly of this build, F7-09).
source: D4 of F7-09 (AMD RDNA ISA reference guides) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: on RDNA, a block made of two compute units that work together.
analogy: two neighbouring sections of the graphics wing sharing some equipment.
precise: the curriculum's vocabulary table (13.1) says that on RDNA, CUs pair into Workgroup Processors; what is shared and how workgroups are placed is to be read in the RDNA ISA guide.
source: D4 of F7-09 (AMD RDNA ISA reference guides) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the chance that the lanes of one wave disagree about a branch.
analogy: the chance that a row contains at least one red bowl.
precise: for lanes that take a rare side independently with probability p, a wave of w lanes runs the rare side with probability 1 − (1 − p)^w; wider waves diverge more often (model of F7-09 Listing 1).
source: arithmetic model, F7-09 run R1

simple: a register that holds one value for every lane of a wave.
analogy: one hand of every helper in the row.
precise: a 32-bit register of the vector register file with one copy per lane; v_ instructions use VGPRs; a kernel's VGPR count is fixed at compile time (.vgpr_count, resource report) and limits occupancy.
source: D2 of F7-10 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) and D5 (LLVM AMDGPU user guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); compiler output of this build

simple: a register that holds one value for the whole wave.
analogy: the row's shared notepad.
precise: a 32-bit register of the scalar register file, one copy per wave; s_ instructions use SGPRs; uniform values such as kernel-argument pointers and loop counters live there.
source: D2 of F7-10 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: on CDNA targets, a second set of per-lane registers made for matrix instructions.
analogy: a tray each helper can also hold, meant for the matrix machine.
precise: accumulation VGPRs (a0, a1, …) used by MFMA instructions, moved with v_accvgpr_read/v_accvgpr_write; the gfx90a compiler also uses them as spill space and counts them with VGPRs for occupancy (F7-10 R2, R3).
source: D2 of F7-10 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many waves can be resident on one SIMD at the same time.
analogy: how many rows fit at one counter.
precise: the number of waves per SIMD that the scarcest resource allows: wave slots, VGPRs (allocated in granules), LDS per workgroup and further limits; the compiler reports it as "Occupancy [waves/SIMD]". The gfx90a step edges in F7-10 were inferred from compiler output, not read in a document.
source: D2 of F7-10 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); compiler output of this build

simple: a value the compiler could not keep in a register, stored to memory and loaded back.
analogy: a bowl put down on a shelf in the far pantry.
precise: the compiler stores the register to the wave's private scratch memory (buffer_store_dword marked "Folded Spill" in this build's gfx90a code) and reloads it; the resource report gives "VGPRs Spill" and "ScratchSize".
source: D5 of F7-10 (LLVM AMDGPU user guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); compiler output of this build

simple: a promise written on a kernel about the largest workgroup it will get, and optionally how many waves per SIMD you want.
analogy: telling the building "my groups are small", so each helper can get more hands.
precise: in HIP 5.7, __launch_bounds__(N) expands to amdgpu_flat_work_group_size(1, N) and __launch_bounds__(N, M) adds amdgpu_waves_per_eu(M): the second argument means waves per execution unit, not CUDA's minimum blocks per multiprocessor.
source: HIP 5.7 header (read in this build)

simple: AMD's fast on-chip memory shared by the work-items of one workgroup.
analogy: the table in the middle of a group of rows.
precise: a software-managed memory in each CU holding HIP __shared__ variables, accessed with ds_ instructions; its size per workgroup is .group_segment_fixed_size.
source: D2 of F7-11 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one of several independent parts of the LDS, each able to serve one word at a time.
analogy: one drawer of the table.
precise: consecutive 4-byte words lie in consecutive banks; lanes needing different words of one bank are served in several passes (a bank conflict), lanes reading the same word are served together; the bank count is a product fact.
source: D2 of F7-11 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one round in which each bank hands out at most one word.
analogy: one moment at the drawers.
precise: in F7-11's model, the passes of one wave-wide access are the sum, over lane groups served together, of the largest number of distinct words one bank must deliver.
source: model of F7-11 Listing 1

simple: unused words added at the end of each row so a column spreads over the banks.
analogy: one empty slot at the end of every row of drawers.
precise: declaring tile[64][65] instead of tile[64][64]: a column then has word stride 65 and hits every bank in the 32-bank model; costs extra LDS and can lower occupancy (F7-11 lab: 4 to 3 waves per SIMD).
source: model and compiler output of F7-11

simple: storing each row's elements in a shuffled order so a column lands in different banks without extra space.
analogy: each row puts its ingredients in the drawers in a different order, by a rule everybody knows.
precise: storing element (r, c) at word 64r + (c XOR r); spreads a column like padding does with no extra bytes, at the cost of extra address instructions (v_xor_b32 in F7-11's ISA).
source: model and compiler output of F7-11

simple: the instruction where all waves of a workgroup wait for each other.
analogy: everyone at the table stops until the whole group has put its ingredients down.
precise: the workgroup barrier that HIP's __syncthreads() compiles to on gfx90a; HIP 5.7 implements __syncthreads() as __barrier(__CLK_LOCAL_MEM_FENCE).
source: HIP 5.7 header (read in this build); compiler output of this build

simple: each lane reads a value from another lane of the same wave.
analogy: passing a bowl a fixed number of places along the row.
precise: HIP 5.7's __shfl, __shfl_up, __shfl_down and __shfl_xor, width defaulting to warpSize, built on ds_bpermute_b32 on AMD; a lane whose source is outside its segment gets its own value back.
source: HIP 5.7 header (read in this build)

simple: every lane answers yes or no, and the wave gets one number whose bits are the answers.
analogy: raising hands; the leader writes one tick per helper.
precise: HIP 5.7's __ballot(predicate) returns unsigned long long with bit l set for active lane l whose predicate is non-zero (__builtin_amdgcn_uicmp).
source: HIP 5.7 header (read in this build)

simple: a number with one bit per lane, saying which lanes are meant.
analogy: the line of ticks, one per helper.
precise: a bit set indexed by lane, 64 bits on wave64; EXEC, VCC and ballot results are lane masks; HIP 5.7's __lanemask_lt/gt/eq return uint64_t. Storing one in 32 bits compiles without a warning and loses lanes 32–63 (F7-12 lab).
source: HIP 5.7 header (read in this build)

simple: how many bits of a number are 1.
analogy: counting the raised hands.
precise: HIP 5.7's __popcll(unsigned long long) is __builtin_popcountll; __popc counts 32 bits only; on gfx90a it became s_bcnt1_i32_b64 or v_bcnt_u32_b32 in this build.
source: HIP 5.7 header (read in this build); compiler output

simple: packing the lanes that keep a value into consecutive places, with no gaps.
analogy: keepers putting jars on the shelf in order.
precise: each keeping lane writes to slot popcount(ballot & lanemask_lt); the number kept is popcount(ballot).
source: F7-12 Listing 1 (run in this build)

simple: the AMD instruction that lets each lane fetch a 32-bit value from any lane of its wave.
analogy: each helper names the helper whose bowl they want.
precise: a backward permute of the LDS hardware taking a per-lane byte address (lane × 4) and returning the source lane's value, without allocating LDS memory; HIP 5.7 builds every __shfl variant on it.
source: D2 of F7-12 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); HIP 5.7 header

simple: the machine language of AMD GPUs.
analogy: the house language of the second building's recipe cards.
precise: the instruction set documented per generation in AMD's ISA reference guides (gfx90a: the MI200 / CDNA2 guide); the LLVM AMDGPU back end emits it as assembly text and as binary in a code object; there is no separate virtual ISA in the HIP-on-AMD flow of this build.
source: D2 and D5 of F7-13 (MI200 ISA guide; LLVM AMDGPU user guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the file that holds a GPU's compiled kernels for one target.
analogy: the bound book of house-language cards for one building.
precise: an ELF file for the AMD GPU architecture with one symbol per kernel, one 64-byte kernel descriptor per kernel and metadata in an ELF note; a HIP executable bundles one per --offload-arch target.
source: D5 of F7-13 (LLVM AMDGPU user guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); tool output of this build

simple: a small block of settings the hardware reads before it starts a kernel.
analogy: the header card of a recipe: how many hands, how much table, where the first line is.
precise: a 64-byte structure (<kernel>.kd) built from the .amdhsa_* directives: LDS and scratch sizes, kernel-argument size, user SGPRs, register allocation, floating-point modes.
source: D5 of F7-13 (LLVM AMDGPU user guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the memory block that holds a kernel's arguments.
analogy: the order slip clipped to the recipe card.
precise: a buffer whose address the kernel receives in an SGPR pair (s[6:7] in F7-13's dot kernel) and reads with scalar loads at fixed offsets; its size is .kernarg_segment_size.
source: D5 of F7-13 (LLVM AMDGPU user guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a tag that tells which of two binary forms an instruction uses.
analogy: a short card and a long card for the same step.
precise: the 32-bit and 64-bit encodings of vector instructions; the 64-bit form allows more operands, such as a compare result in an SGPR pair instead of VCC.
source: D2 of F7-13 (AMD Instinct MI200 ISA reference guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); disassembly of this build

simple: one file that carries host code and device code for several GPU targets.
analogy: one folder holding the recipe books for several buildings.
precise: the clang offload bundle inside a HIP executable, listing a host entry and one code object per --offload-arch target (F7-13 lab: host, gfx1100, gfx90a).
source: LLVM documentation — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); tool output of this build

simple: AMD's command-line profiler for traces, kernel statistics and hardware counters.
analogy: the observer at the door with a clipboard.
precise: the ROCm profiling tool named in the curriculum's vocabulary table (with its predecessor rocprof); options and output formats are in its documentation. Not installed in this build.
source: D7 of F7-14 (ROCm profiler documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: AMD's tool for a deep look at single kernels and how close they come to the hardware's limits.
analogy: the observer who sits at one table and counts everything.
precise: the per-kernel analysis tool formerly named Omniperf, with speed-of-light, memory-chart and roofline views built from hardware counters. Not installed in this build.
source: D7 of F7-14 (ROCm Compute Profiler documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: AMD's tool for one timeline of the whole program: host threads, API calls, copies and kernels.
analogy: the observer who films the whole street.
precise: the system-wide tracing and sampling profiler formerly named Omnitrace. Not installed in this build.
source: D7 of F7-14 (ROCm Systems Profiler documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number a profiler computes from raw counts and time, such as GB/s.
analogy: "jars per minute", from "jars" and "minutes".
precise: a formula over counters and duration: bandwidth = bytes / time, FLOP/s = operations / time, arithmetic intensity = operations / bytes, percentage of the roofline at that intensity (F7-14 Listing 2).
source: F7-14 Listing 2 (run in this build, invented inputs)

simple: the list of kernels with start and end times, drawn on a time axis.
analogy: the film of the street, frame by frame.
precise: a record of each dispatch's start and end timestamps, with host API calls and threads in a systems profiler; GPU busy share, gaps and overlap are read from it (F7-14 Listing 3, a model).
source: F7-14 Listing 3 (run in this build, invented durations)
